authority: owner ledger 2417 (closure parent approved), 2459 (start); coordinator rulings of 2026-11-11

scopeDecisions.decision: Node.js v2 onTaskDispatched in us-central1, one pinned SDK (firebase-functions 7.3.2, firebase-admin 14.3.0 request shape). Gen1, Python (FUNCTIONS-PYTHON owns its Tasks row), other regions, extension queues, App Engine and pull queues are excluded.

Production is observed through eight functions deployed with the pinned firebase-tools (so the queue settings are the CLI's mapping) and the Cloud Tasks REST API against the queues the deploy made. A queue id cannot be created again for days after a delete, so every run suffixes the function ids with six hexadecimal digits of its run id and deletes its queues and functions at cleanup.
At most US$4 for the parent including recovery: two recordings and at most three attempts, inside the US$10 per observation task (coordinator ruling 5).

The strict profile follows the recordings. A production behaviour that makes local tests worse (long default dispatch deadline waits, names kept forever, backoff delays) becomes a per-key development default that productionExact restores (coordinator ruling 6, HOSTING ruling 23). The emulator profile never refuses more than firebase-tools 15.28.2 and makes no production claim.

A time-dependent condition is compared by bounds that two recordings support (a lower bound, an upper bound, an order, a count), never by exact milliseconds, and the judge states the tolerance it used.

conditions.description: The status and shape of a successful createTask answer: the task name form, the defaults of scheduleTime, dispatchDeadline and httpMethod, what the BASIC and FULL views return, and what the Admin SDK ignores.
The status and the google.rpc.Status of a refused createTask: a missing task or httpRequest, an unknown field, a queue that does not exist, and the code the Admin SDK maps each to.
Which task ids and names are accepted: characters, the 500 and 501 character boundary, an empty id, a name that points at another queue or project, and a punctuation-only id.
A task id that is still in a queue: the answer to a second createTask (409 ALREADY_EXISTS), the same id on another queue, and the answer of getTask.
A task id that has finished or been deleted, inside the reuse window: the answer to a createTask with the same id. The expiry of the window is a separate condition.

The end of the reuse window of a task id (documented as about one hour). Not part of stage 1: a stage 2 packet of about 70 minutes, only if stage 1 leaves it unsettled (coordinator ruling 4 of 2026-11-11).
conditions.reason: The end of the reuse window was not observed: the window is documented as about one hour and strict under productionExact refuses a name for 3600 seconds after it finished or was deleted. A stage 2 packet of about 70 minutes would record the expiry; stage 1 leaves the refusal inside the window recorded, so the packet is recommended against unless the coordinator wants the length measured (ruling 4).

conditions.description: scheduleTime in the past, now, close, in the nanosecond and numeric-offset forms, on both sides of the 30 day limit, far away, and malformed (text, no zone, a leap second).
A delivery is not earlier than its scheduleTime, and the X-CloudTasks-TaskETA header of a scheduled and an unscheduled task.
The range of dispatchDeadline (14s, 15s, 1800s, 1801s, a fraction, no unit, negative, zero), its default in the createTask answer, and a delivery that outlasts it.
The largest task body accepted (1,000,000 and 1,100,000 byte bodies) and how task headers that the service owns are treated.

The delivered request: method, path, the set of header names, the fixed header values, the X-CloudTasks-* values of a first delivery and of retries, the user agent, the authorization scheme, and which task headers win.
The delivered body: byte for byte what the task carried (non-ASCII, member order, white space, an empty data object, 100,000 bytes), and the data the SDK hands the handler.
The name and X-CloudTasks-TaskName of a task created without an id.
The queue settings a deployed task queue function ends up with (rateLimits and retryConfig), read back from Cloud Tasks for the default and for every declared option.
conditions.reason: The queue settings are read back with getQueue, which is the Cloud Tasks queue management API: neither fireemu nor the official emulator serves it (coordinator ruling 3). The settings read from production are recorded in both recordings (the queue-* cases) and their effects are compared by retry-backoff-schedule, retry-limits and max-concurrent-dispatches.

conditions.description: Which handler answers are retried (500, 429, 503, 400, 404, a timeout), and the retry headers: retryCount, executionCount, previousResponse, retryReason.
The delay before each retry for a minBackoff, a maxBackoff and a maxDoublings (bounds, not exact times).
A task is dropped after maxAttempts attempts, or when maxRetrySeconds has passed, and nothing is delivered afterwards.
At most maxConcurrentDispatches deliveries of a queue at the same time (1 and 2).
The dispatch rate of a queue with maxDispatchesPerSecond 1: the first deliveries, the spacing, and any burst.
conditions.reason: The program sent the eight tasks of the rate queue about 1.4 seconds apart in both production runs, so the limit never held a task back and no spacing or burst was observed; the local limiter spaces them one second apart. Rate and burst are not claimed (the rate cases carry no timing claim).

conditions.description: The answers of deleteTask: a task in the queue, a task that never existed, and a task that has finished.

The virtual clock, the Run now control, queue statistics, the await-idle scope, the memory limits and the Host guard: local properties with local evidence, no production recording (as the SCHEDULED-FUNCTIONS fireemu-only rows).
Every comparison of this record reproduced on the final binary (integratedRegression).
An independent review approves the record.

excludedFromParent.reason: CLI deploy behaviour, IAM enqueuer bindings and Cloud Run settings: only the queue settings are read back.
createQueue, updateQueue, pause, purge, getTask and listTasks as an API: used for setup and read-back, no claim that fireemu implements them.
Python task queue functions: FUNCTIONS-PYTHON owns the tasks-events row.
TaskOptions.uri: the local daemon refuses an arbitrary outbound request on purpose.
The value and verification of the OIDC token: only its scheme and segment count are compared.
Delivery order across tasks (Cloud Tasks is best effort) and exact times.
Cold start, scaling, billing and quota.

limitations: Two production recordings (stage 1) back the verified conditions; the parent stays IMPLEMENTING until an independent review approves the record.
The in-memory Cloud Tasks of the recorder's tests is a model of documented rules, not an observation; no judge accepts a shape from it.

A queue id cannot be created again for days after a delete (400 'existed too recently', measured 2026-11-07), so each attempt of a recording needs new function ids and a failed attempt costs a deploy.

The reuse window of a task id is refused for 3600 seconds under strict productionExact (`functions.taskNameReuse` `production`, documented as about one hour); its expiry was not observed. The default profile frees a finished name at once, and an explicit key wins over productionExact.

Production's default queue retry config comes from a recording: the default queue of a function that declared no retry options read back (getQueue, both runs) with maxAttempts 100, minBackoff 0.100 s, maxBackoff 3600 s and maxDoublings 16 and no maxRetryDuration, the Cloud Tasks documentation's defaults. `functions.taskRetryDefaults` `production` (selected by productionExact) fills maxAttempts 100 for a field the function does not declare; the default profile keeps the official emulator's 3 attempts, and a declared value is always kept.
outOfScope: Production deployment parity of task queue functions beyond the queue settings.
No condition is promoted from official-emulator behaviour or documentation alone.
